meta.title: Alex's Robot Game
meta.textType: functional: an email with game instructions and screen feedback

paragraphs: On Wednesday, December sixteenth, Tom and Ben sat on the sofa in the living room. It was four o'clock, and the laptop stood on the low table. Pip lay next to the table with his red ball. Tom opened a new email from his pen pal Alex. Alex liked robots and computer games. The email had instructions and a picture of a small gray robot in a maze. The game was called "ROBOT RUN."

Tom read the email out loud, and Ben listened. "Dear Tom, I invented a robot game, and it is ready." "It is free online." "The robot is in a maze on a space station." "It must find the exit and the rocket." "Step one: download the software." "Step two: click START." "Step three: type the password, which is robot." "Step four: use the arrow keys to move the robot to the exit." "If the robot touches a wall, you will lose a life." Tom downloaded the software and clicked START. A box on the screen asked for a password. He typed the word robot, and five dots appeared.

Tom read on. "Tom, there is a paper version for you and Ben, too." "Print the board at the end of this email." "Put a counter on START." "Throw the number cube and move your counter." "If you land on a red square, you will go back two squares." "How often do you play computer games, Tom?" "Best wishes, Alex." Tom printed the board, because Ben liked board games. The path went from START to FINISH, and some squares were red. Ben took the gray robot counter and put it on START.

Tom wanted to try the laptop game first. He sat in front of the screen and pressed the arrow keys. The robot touched a wall, and the screen said, "Try again." Tom started again and moved the robot slowly to the exit. A voice from the speaker said, "Great! Level two." "Can you reach level five?" asked Ben. "I think so," said Tom, "but the maze is hard." Then Pip jumped on the sofa and stepped on the keyboard. The robot hit a wall, and the speaker said, "Try again."

Ben laughed and lifted Pip off the keyboard. "Pip wants to play, too," said Ben. Tom opened a new email and wrote a reply. "Dear Alex, thank you for your game." "I play computer games two times a week." "If I reach level five, I will send you a photo." "Ben and I are playing the paper version on Saturday." "Best wishes, Tom."
text.summary: Tom and Ben read an email from Alex with the steps of his new robot game. Tom plays on the laptop and hears the screen answers, and Ben tries the paper board.
